html:
The kula ring is a ceremonial exchange among the Trobriand and other Massim islands of eastern Papua New Guinea. Men sail between islands to trade shell necklaces in one direction around the ring and shell armbands in the other.

The valuables are never kept for long. Holding a famous piece brings fame, and each exchange binds partners on distant islands, along with ordinary trade in food and goods.

The anthropologist Bronisław Malinowski described it in Argonauts of the Western Pacific in 1922, after living on the Trobriands during the First World War. The book shaped the study of gifts and exchange, starting with Marcel Mauss's The Gift. The kula is still practised on the Trobriand Islands and their neighbours.
